title: Hydrogen uptake of reduced graphene oxide and graphene sheets decorated with Fe nanoclusters
material_description: GO | graphene oxide by modified Staudenmaier's method: graphite powder (99.99%, Sigma-Aldrich) oxidized in conc. H2SO4/HNO3 with KClO3 (95 h, room temperature), washed with dilute HCl and water, dried at 40 C under vacuum 5 h; graphite oxide thermally exfoliated at 1050 C under Ar for 30 s (quartz tube)
functional_groups: oxygen-containing functional groups (large amount; types not specified)
source_location: main p.7 (journal p.8317), Table 3, row GO, 300 K / 50 bar
notes: Only H2 value for GO in the paper (no plotted isotherm). Printed only in wt%. BET range: P/P0 < 0.5 (text, stated for all 'graphene samples', a term the paper defines to include GO). BET 304 m2/g (text and Table 3); skeletal density 1.85 g/cc (He gas probing). Method notes: volumetric four-channel Sieverts apparatus (Advanced Materials Corporation, USA; no model named); about 25 mg sample (printed 'About 25 mg'); outgassed at 523 K for about two hours under high vacuum of the order of 1e-7 torr (stored 249.85 C, 2 h, 1.33322e-5 Pa); H2 purity 99.999% ('All gases used for sorption analysis are of 99.999% purity'); skeletal density by helium gas probing, but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described=false; measuring lab = corresponding author's group (paper says 'our apparatus' and does not name the laboratory where H2 was measured); basis not named (paper only says He/H2 comparison is 'the characteristic feature of no excess adsorption'), volumetric default -> excess.

source_location: main p.6 (journal p.8316), Fig. 6, series (C) Adsorption at 77 K (filled blue triangles), CR-GO
notes: archive: HYC-0013_fig6_C_CRGO_77K_ads.json. Digitized marker centre (pixel 803.5,1028.9 on the 4x enlarged crop, 68 px); uptake read on the left axis (cm3(STP)/g), wt% = W1 computed (right-hand wt% axis also printed; its scale matches W1). isotherm_point_count approximate: about 94 adsorption markers (C: 83 single markers digitized + 5 unseparated merged blobs of about 2-3 markers) + about 78 open desorption markers (D, counted visually). BET range: P/P0 < 0.5 (text); 'very good fit between the ranges 0.05 to 0.3' (text and SI); Fig. S3(b) 'Fit Range: 0.058661 to 0.344698'. BET 9 m2/g (text, Table 3; Fig. S3(b) prints 8.804491 m2/g); skeletal density 2.0 g/cc. Method notes: volumetric four-channel Sieverts apparatus (Advanced Materials Corporation, USA; no model named); about 25 mg sample (printed 'About 25 mg'); outgassed at 523 K for about two hours under high vacuum of the order of 1e-7 torr (stored 249.85 C, 2 h, 1.33322e-5 Pa); H2 purity 99.999% ('All gases used for sorption analysis are of 99.999% purity'); skeletal density by helium gas probing, but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described=false; measuring lab = corresponding author's group (paper says 'our apparatus' and does not name the laboratory where H2 was measured); basis not named (paper only says He/H2 comparison is 'the characteristic feature of no excess adsorption'), volumetric default -> excess.

source_location: main p.6 (journal p.8316), Fig. 6, series (C) Adsorption at 77 K (filled blue triangles), CR-GO
notes: archive: HYC-0013_fig6_C_CRGO_77K_ads.json. Digitized marker centre (pixel 1328.6,641.5 on the 4x enlarged crop, 80 px); uptake read on the left axis (cm3(STP)/g), wt% = W1 computed (right-hand wt% axis also printed; its scale matches W1). isotherm_point_count approximate: about 94 adsorption markers (C: 83 single markers digitized + 5 unseparated merged blobs of about 2-3 markers) + about 78 open desorption markers (D, counted visually). BET range: P/P0 < 0.5 (text); 'very good fit between the ranges 0.05 to 0.3' (text and SI); Fig. S3(b) 'Fit Range: 0.058661 to 0.344698'. BET 9 m2/g (text, Table 3; Fig. S3(b) prints 8.804491 m2/g); skeletal density 2.0 g/cc. Method notes: volumetric four-channel Sieverts apparatus (Advanced Materials Corporation, USA; no model named); about 25 mg sample (printed 'About 25 mg'); outgassed at 523 K for about two hours under high vacuum of the order of 1e-7 torr (stored 249.85 C, 2 h, 1.33322e-5 Pa); H2 purity 99.999% ('All gases used for sorption analysis are of 99.999% purity'); skeletal density by helium gas probing, but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described=false; measuring lab = corresponding author's group (paper says 'our apparatus' and does not name the laboratory where H2 was measured); basis not named (paper only says He/H2 comparison is 'the characteristic feature of no excess adsorption'), volumetric default -> excess.

material_description: Graphene nanosheets decorated with Fe | Fe-GS: graphene sheets decorated with Fe nanoclusters, deposited on the chamber wall by dc arc discharge (~100 A, 25 V, ~300 torr Ar, 8-10 min) between a pure graphite cathode and a graphite anode impregnated with Fe nanopowder (APS 10-30 nm, 99.9%, Alfa Aesar); Fe loading not stated
source_location: main p.7 (journal p.8317), Fig. 7, series (C) Adsorption at 77 K (filled blue up-triangles), Fe-GS
notes: archive: HYC-0013_fig7_C_FeGS_77K_ads.json. Digitized marker centre (pixel 1675.1,209.3 on the 4x enlarged crop, 121 px); uptake read on the left axis (cm3(STP)/g), wt% = W1 computed (right-hand wt% axis also printed; its scale matches W1). isotherm_point_count approximate: about 93 adsorption markers (C: 80 single markers digitized + 6 unseparated merged blobs) + about 61 open desorption markers (D, counted visually). BET range: P/P0 < 0.5 (text); 'very good fit between the ranges 0.05 to 0.3' (text and SI); Fig. S3(c) 'Fit Range: 0.060738 to 0.341713'. BET 190 m2/g (text, Table 3; Fig. S3(c) prints 190.267084 m2/g); skeletal density 1.05 g/cc. Method notes: volumetric four-channel Sieverts apparatus (Advanced Materials Corporation, USA; no model named); about 25 mg sample (printed 'About 25 mg'); outgassed at 523 K for about two hours under high vacuum of the order of 1e-7 torr (stored 249.85 C, 2 h, 1.33322e-5 Pa); H2 purity 99.999% ('All gases used for sorption analysis are of 99.999% purity'); skeletal density by helium gas probing, but the paper does not say how the free volume was determined, so calibration_described=false; measuring lab = corresponding author's group (paper says 'our apparatus' and does not name the laboratory where H2 was measured); basis not named (paper only says He/H2 comparison is 'the characteristic feature of no excess adsorption'), volumetric default -> excess.
